title: Jake's bank created $20,000 out of thin air

beats.text: Jake just borrowed 20,000 dollars for a car. His bank didn't lend him anyone's savings. It created the money.
Here's how a bank makes money from nothing, and why it can't do it forever.
When the loan is approved, the bank just types 20,000 into his account. Brand new money.
Not a conspiracy theory. The Bank of England explained it in 2014.
But there's a catch. When Jake pays the loan back, that money disappears.
And banks need borrowers who'll repay, while the Fed steers what borrowing costs.
So most money isn't printed. It's typed. Did you know your bank could do that?
